pathway.title: MOLINA HEALTHCARE, INC. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Earnings, not debt, are the weak link. EBITDA built by Financial foundation fell from USD 1,893 million in FY2024 to USD 976 million in FY2025 and USD 333 million over the last twelve months, while revenue was USD 40,650 million, USD 45,426 million and USD 44,127 million, so the damage is margin. The medical care ratio rose to 92.1% for the nine months of 2026 from 90.8%, the Medicaid ratio to 92.6% from 91.2%, and on current-year costs alone to 93.22% from 91.15%, because USD 352 million of favourable reserve development flattered the reported figure. State and federal premium rates are set annually, so the company cannot reprice quickly, and each percentage point of the ratio is worth USD 415.88 million of EBITDA. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 32–33; calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6

Liquidity buys time but is held in the wrong place. Unrestricted cash and investments of USD 8,579 million exceed claims and government settlements owed of USD 6,129 million by only USD 2,450 million, and most of it sits in regulated plans; the parent held USD 608 million, which is USD 3,163 million less than the debt it owes. Dividends of about USD 170 million can be paid without approval, which is 88.83% of the annual coupons on the notes, so servicing them relies on regulators approving more. Net cash passed up to the parent covered its interest expense 2.84x in FY2025 but 1.24x in the first nine months of 2026. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36, 39; calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C10

Refinancing is a 2028 question, not a 2026 one, but replacement debt would cost more. The first maturity is USD 800 million on 2028-06-15, followed by USD 650 million in 2030 and USD 2,350 million across 2031 to 2033, and the USD 1,250 million revolver is undrawn to 2030-11-20. The issuer-stated fair value of the notes is 93.84% of principal, and 86.93% for the 2032 notes; S&P rates them BB- and Moody's Ba2; replacing the 2028 notes at the coupon carried by the 2031 notes would add USD 17.00 million of annual interest. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13

The business model concentrates risk in one program and four states. Medicaid was 74.89% of premium revenue and the Texas, California, Washington and New York contracts together 40.23%; state contracts run three to five years, can be ended by either party and are rebid, and membership at 2026-09-30 was 13.61% below a year earlier, with Marketplace down 59.24% since year-end. Management expects the federal budget law to cut premium by 2% to 3% a year through 2029, and the premium it states for the new Florida contract is hard to reconcile with its enrolment, so replacement revenue is uncertain. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–31; calculation C8

Financial policy is a medium governance risk rather than a rating driver on its own. There is no sponsor and no dividend; the parent bought back USD 1,000 million of stock in each of 2024 and 2025, 211.86% of FY2025 net income in the latest year, in a year when it also borrowed USD 1,100 million, and nothing in 2026. The covenant interest cover test was lowered temporarily to 1.75x on 2026-02-04 for reasons not given, and headroom cannot be measured because the agreement is not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; calculation C15

Cash generation is a working-capital story, not an earnings story. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 535 million in FY2025 and an inflow of USD 629 million in the first nine months of 2026, of which USD 297 million came from working-capital movements; by quarter it was USD 1,082 million, then outflows of USD 294 million and USD 159 million. Capital spending of USD 101 million is small, so free cash flow follows the timing of settlements with governments rather than earnings. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_moh1q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-07-22_moh2q26_er.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C4

runs.text: The strengths are a maturity profile with nothing due before 2028 and an undrawn revolver, which means a refinancing event is not the near-term test; low capital intensity, with capital spending of USD 101 million against USD 45,426 million of revenue; the suspension of buybacks and the rise in parent cash to USD 608 million; a record of renewing and winning state contracts, in management's words; and audited, transparent reporting that lets creditors see where the weakness is. The weaknesses are margins that depend on a ratio the company does not set and that has moved from 90.8% to 92.1% in a year; leverage of 11.32x on last-twelve-months EBITDA with accrued interest cover of 1.56x; concentration, with Medicaid at 74.89% and four states at 40.23% of premium revenue; a parent that relies on subsidiary dividends and holds a small part of group cash; and shrinking membership with policy headwinds through 2029. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C9

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no sponsor transaction. The new debt in the period is the November 2025 refinancing: the company sold USD 850 million of senior unsecured notes due 2031 in a private offering on 2025-11-20, used the proceeds to repay USD 740 million of term loan debt and for general corporate purposes, and replaced its revolving facility with a USD 1.25 billion facility ending 2030-11-20 under a new credit agreement whose terms the company calls substantially similar except for covenants amended in its favour. The credit agreement was amended on 2026-02-04 to lower the minimum interest cover test temporarily, and no further debt was issued in 2026. The only acquisition in the period was ConnectiCare, bought for USD 350 million of cash and closed on 2025-02-01.

fields.value: Financial foundation for MOLINA HEALTHCARE, INC. (issuer id moh), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated statements in US dollars for FY2023 to FY2025 and the nine months to 2026-09-30, the debt, cash and liquidity tables, and the leverage and cover ratios built from them, with the parent-only statements used for the perimeter of the senior notes. Where the filings print no EBITDA, it is built from operating income and depreciation and amortization and labelled as calculated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings, far more than debt, drive the credit risk: last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 333 million against USD 3,771 million of parent senior notes is reported leverage of 11.32x, up from 1.54x at FY2024, so creditors rely on cash and distant maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The group holds net cash on its balance sheet (cash of USD 4,479 million against debt of USD 3,771 million), but the notes sit at the parent, which held only about USD 608 million, while USD 6,129 million of claims and government settlements are owed out of group cash and investments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage has risen mainly because earnings fell, with new debt a smaller cause. EBITDA, which the issuer does not print and which is built here as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, fell from USD 1,893 million in FY2024 to USD 976 million in FY2025 and to USD 333 million over the last twelve months. Debt rose from USD 2,923 million at FY2024 to USD 3,771 million at 2026-09-30, USD 848 million more after the senior notes due 2031 were issued in November 2025, but holding debt at its FY2024 level would still give 8.78x on the latest EBITDA, so most of the rise to 11.32x comes from the denominator.

fields.value: Revenue has not fallen far (USD 40,650 million in FY2024, USD 45,426 million in FY2025 and USD 44,127 million over the last twelve months), so the damage is margin. The medical care ratio, medical costs as a share of premium revenue, was 92.1% for the nine months of 2026 against 90.8% a year earlier and 89.1% in FY2024. Because EBITDA is a thin residual of USD 41,588 million of last-twelve-months premium revenue, an increase of 0.80 percentage points in that ratio with premiums unchanged would remove all of it, and each percentage point is worth USD 415.88 million (an analyst sensitivity, not an issuer figure). Creditors therefore carry one cost-trend ratio that state rate-setting, not the company, largely controls.

The rest of the cash sits in regulated health plans that must hold minimum capital of about USD 3.0 billion and may pay only about USD 170 million of dividends without regulatory approval.

fields.value: Much of the cash is working-capital float rather than free liquidity. Medical claims payable of USD 4,988 million and amounts due to government agencies of USD 1,141 million, together USD 6,129 million, are non-interest-bearing obligations that premium cash is held to meet. Against unrestricted cash and investments of USD 8,579 million they leave USD 2,450 million, compared with USD 2,473 million at FY2024 and USD 2,043 million at FY2025. Membership fell 11.46% over the nine months while claims payable rose, so cash would leave to settle older claims if claims payable fell in step with enrolment.

fields.value: Interest is serviced by the parent from cash passed up by regulated subsidiaries, and that support has thinned. The two figures are not defined identically (the quarterly report counts dividends and returns of capital) and dividends are lumpy within a year, so the comparison shows direction, not a precise change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation improved in 2026 for reasons other than earnings. Operating cash flow was USD 629 million for the nine months against an outflow of USD 237 million a year earlier, yet net income fell to USD 112 million from USD 632 million: working-capital movements turned from an outflow of USD 1,082 million to an inflow of USD 297 million, and the issuer attributes this mainly to smaller settlements with government agencies (USD 185 million paid against USD 467 million). The inflow came early: operating cash flow was USD 1,082 million in the first quarter, then an outflow of USD 294 million in the second and USD 159 million in the third, and cash and cash equivalents fell from USD 5,314 million at 2026-03-31 to USD 4,479 million at 2026-09-30. FY2025 operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 535 million (working capital an outflow of USD 1,289 million) and free cash flow after USD 101 million of capital spending an outflow of USD 636 million. Financing outflows of USD 31 million in 2026 were only stock withheld for taxes and other items, so no shares were repurchased, whereas USD 1,000 million was bought in the first nine months of 2025, which removes the biggest discretionary outflow of 2025.

fields.value: All debt is five senior unsecured notes of the parent, with USD 3,800 million of principal and USD 3,771 million of carrying value. Principal falls due as USD 800 million in 2028, USD 650 million in 2030, USD 850 million in 2031 and USD 750 million in each of 2032 and 2033, so nothing is due in 2026 or 2027; the USD 1,250 million revolver is undrawn and ends on 2030-11-20. Finance lease liabilities of USD 179 million are carried outside debt and are excluded from every ratio; adding the USD 209 million of finance leases at FY2025 would lift leverage to 4.07x from 3.86x. No pension, retiree-medical, factoring or supplier-finance obligation is described, and management states that its other agreements hold no material non-cancelable commitments.

fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that the weakest quarter is about to leave the last-twelve-months window. EBITDA for the fourth quarter of 2025, calculated as FY2025 less the nine months, was an outflow of USD 118 million against USD 122 million, USD 185 million and USD 144 million in the first three quarters of 2026, and 2026 guidance implies fourth-quarter 2026 net income of roughly USD 10 million at its minimum against a loss of USD 160 million a year earlier, so last-twelve-months EBITDA should rise at the next report even though the new Florida contract is guided to cost USD 1.50 per share in that quarter. The USD 93 million impairment in the first quarter also depresses the period: before it, last-twelve-months EBITDA would be USD 426 million and EBITDA over accrued interest 2.00x. No note matures before 2028, the USD 1,250 million revolver is undrawn, the securities class action was dismissed with prejudice on 2026-10-20, and the issuer states that every covenant was met at 2026-09-30.

fields.value: Business, transaction, ownership and governance fact pack for MOLINA HEALTHCARE, INC. (issuer id moh), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is what the issuer does, who owns and controls it, which transactions and events shape its credit, and whether governance or capital allocation raises creditor risk. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no sponsor to model, and that cuts both ways. Fourteen registered holders of record (including the depository nominee) hold the common stock, which is listed on the New York Stock Exchange, no cash dividend has ever been paid, and the supplied documents disclose no controlling holder, fee arrangement or related-party payment, so extraction by an owner is not evidenced. The same absence means no sponsor equity stands behind the notes: the parent's own USD 608 million of cash and investments at 2026-09-30 is the only identified buffer, and ownership percentages and board independence are held in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is concentrated in one program and four states, and the contract model gives it little protection. Medicaid was USD 32,240 million of FY2025 premium revenue, and the Texas, California, Washington and New York Medicaid contracts together were USD 17,320 million, or 40.23% of all premium revenue. State contracts run three to five years, can be terminated by either party with or without cause, and are rebid; the Virginia contracts ended on 2025-06-30 after Molina was not an awardee. A loss of any large state contract would remove revenue that fixed costs and USD 3,771 million of parent debt service rely on.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model turns on one ratio the company does not set. Premiums are fixed per member by each state and must be actuarially sound, while the company bears medical cost risk, so cost trend above rate updates lifts the medical care ratio: 92.1% for the nine months of 2026 against 90.8% a year earlier. The reported ratio flatters the trend, because favourable reserve releases of USD 352 million helped it; on current-year costs alone the ratio was 93.22% against 91.15%. With last-twelve-months premium revenue of USD 41,588 million, each percentage point of the ratio is worth USD 415.88 million of earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Membership and revenue are contracting while new contracts are still to arrive. Total membership at 2026-09-30 was 13.61% below the same date a year earlier, with Marketplace down 59.24% since year-end through a deliberate repricing and Medicaid down 4.29%. Management expects the 2025 federal budget law to cut Medicaid premium growth by 2% to 3% a year through 2029 and a further USD 1 billion of Marketplace premium in 2027. New Florida, Illinois and Wisconsin awards start between 2026-10-01 and 2027-01-01 and the Georgia and Texas awards slipped to late 2027 or 2028, so the timing of replacement revenue is uncertain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation favoured buybacks in a year of heavy borrowing and falling earnings, and has since reversed. Share purchases of USD 500 million in the first quarter of 2025 came at an average of USD 297.83 a share and USD 500 million in the third quarter at USD 175.50, in a year when the company also borrowed USD 650 million in the first quarter and USD 1,100 million over the first nine months; the filings do not link the two. Acquisitions were modest by comparison: ConnectiCare for USD 350 million of cash. In FY2025 the parent's buybacks (USD 1,000 million), the acquisition (USD 350 million) and subsidiary contributions (USD 439 million) came to USD 1,789 million against USD 1,823 million of subsidiary dividends and net note proceeds, which left little over for its other outflows, and its cash and investments ended at USD 223 million. In 2026 the company stopped repurchasing, which is creditor-aligned, but an amendment on 2026-02-04 cut the minimum interest cover test to 1.75x for the rest of 2026 for reasons the filings do not give.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for covenant work. The annual accounts carry an unqualified audit opinion and a critical audit matter on the reserve for claims incurred but not paid, which was USD 3,211 million of USD 4,887 million of medical claims payable; management reported effective internal controls with the ConnectiCare business excluded from the assessment. Covenant ratios are stated as met but never printed, and the 2025 securities class action and the related shareholder derivative suit were both dismissed with prejudice in October 2026 with no loss estimate recorded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that nothing here shows value moved to owners at creditors' expense beyond buybacks, and that the buybacks have stopped. Regulated subsidiaries paid USD 985 million of dividends to the parent in FY2025 out of cash above their capital needs, parent cash and investments rose to USD 608 million, the notes were termed out to 2031, and the revolver is undrawn. Management also says it has won 90% of Medicaid re-procurements and 80% of new contracts since 2019, which is its own characterisation and cannot be tested here. The view would improve if buybacks stay suspended after the authority lapses on 2026-12-31 and the medical care ratio falls back toward its FY2025 level of 91.7%. It would worsen if purchases resume while the ratio is above its FY2025 level, if a large-state contract is lost, or if the proxy statement shows a holder with control and a distribution appetite.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for MOLINA HEALTHCARE, INC. (issuer id moh), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's overall credit profile, its strongest support and weakest dimension, the primary downside path and what to monitor, built on the financial statements, the business and governance facts and the source inventory. No rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Molina's fundamental credit is weak at present because earnings no longer cover its leverage: last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 333 million against USD 3,771 million of parent notes is 11.32x, though near-term liquidity and a first maturity in 2028 give noteholders time.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main downside path is medical cost trend outrunning premium rates while membership shrinks: an increase of 0.80 percentage points in the medical care ratio, with premiums unchanged, would remove all last-twelve-months EBITDA, and the USD 352 million of favourable reserve development that helped 2026 cannot be assumed to recur.

fields.value: Earnings, not debt, are the weak link. EBITDA built by Financial foundation fell from USD 1,893 million in FY2024 to USD 976 million in FY2025 and USD 333 million over the last twelve months, while revenue was USD 40,650 million, USD 45,426 million and USD 44,127 million, so the damage is margin. The medical care ratio rose to 92.1% for the nine months of 2026 from 90.8%, the Medicaid ratio to 92.6% from 91.2%, and on current-year costs alone to 93.22% from 91.15%, because USD 352 million of favourable reserve development flattered the reported figure. State and federal premium rates are set annually, so the company cannot reprice quickly, and each percentage point of the ratio is worth USD 415.88 million of EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity buys time but is held in the wrong place. Unrestricted cash and investments of USD 8,579 million exceed claims and government settlements owed of USD 6,129 million by only USD 2,450 million, and most of it sits in regulated plans; the parent held USD 608 million, which is USD 3,163 million less than the debt it owes. Dividends of about USD 170 million can be paid without approval, which is 88.83% of the annual coupons on the notes, so servicing them relies on regulators approving more. Net cash passed up to the parent covered its interest expense 2.84x in FY2025 but 1.24x in the first nine months of 2026.

fields.value: Refinancing is a 2028 question, not a 2026 one, but replacement debt would cost more. The first maturity is USD 800 million on 2028-06-15, followed by USD 650 million in 2030 and USD 2,350 million across 2031 to 2033, and the USD 1,250 million revolver is undrawn to 2030-11-20. The issuer-stated fair value of the notes is 93.84% of principal, and 86.93% for the 2032 notes; S&P rates them BB- and Moody's Ba2; replacing the 2028 notes at the coupon carried by the 2031 notes would add USD 17.00 million of annual interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business model concentrates risk in one program and four states. Medicaid was 74.89% of premium revenue and the Texas, California, Washington and New York contracts together 40.23%; state contracts run three to five years, can be ended by either party and are rebid, and membership at 2026-09-30 was 13.61% below a year earlier, with Marketplace down 59.24% since year-end. Management expects the federal budget law to cut premium by 2% to 3% a year through 2029, and the premium it states for the new Florida contract is hard to reconcile with its enrolment, so replacement revenue is uncertain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is a medium governance risk rather than a rating driver on its own. There is no sponsor and no dividend; the parent bought back USD 1,000 million of stock in each of 2024 and 2025, 211.86% of FY2025 net income in the latest year, in a year when it also borrowed USD 1,100 million, and nothing in 2026. The covenant interest cover test was lowered temporarily to 1.75x on 2026-02-04 for reasons not given, and headroom cannot be measured because the agreement is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is a working-capital story, not an earnings story. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 535 million in FY2025 and an inflow of USD 629 million in the first nine months of 2026, of which USD 297 million came from working-capital movements; by quarter it was USD 1,082 million, then outflows of USD 294 million and USD 159 million. Capital spending of USD 101 million is small, so free cash flow follows the timing of settlements with governments rather than earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weak assessment is that the worst quarter is leaving the window. EBITDA for the fourth quarter of 2025 was an outflow of USD 118 million against USD 144 million in the third quarter of 2026, and 2026 guidance implies fourth-quarter net income of roughly USD 10 million, so last-twelve-months EBITDA should rise at the next report even though the new Florida contract is guided to cost USD 1.50 per share in that quarter. Before the USD 93 million impairment, last-twelve-months EBITDA would have been USD 426 million and EBITDA over accrued interest 2.00x. Management says medical cost trend appears to be plateauing and 2027 rate updates are strong, which is its own view and untested here. Nothing matures before 2028 and the revolver is undrawn.

fields.value: The view would improve if the medical care ratio returns toward its FY2025 level of 91.7% without reserve releases, if parent cash keeps rising from USD 608 million, or if the credit agreement shows wide headroom under the interest cover test. It would worsen if the ratio keeps rising, if the Florida start-up costs more than guided, if buybacks resume under the USD 500 million authority that lapses on 2026-12-31, or if a large-state contract is lost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Molina is a pure-play manager of government-funded health plans that serves 21 states, so its cash flow depends on state and federal budgets rather than on consumers. Medicaid is 74.89% of premium revenue, Medicare 14.48% and Marketplace 10.42% in FY2025, and Medicaid has risen to 78.30% of premium for the nine months of 2026 as Marketplace shrinks. Contracts are short and terminable, which gives visibility of a few years at most and exposes revenue to rebids: the Virginia contracts ended on 2025-06-30. The consequence for creditors is that debt service capacity is only as durable as the next procurement cycle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_moh-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 14–16; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer is a listed public corporation with no sponsor and no controlling holder disclosed; the notes are obligations of the parent only, with no subsidiary guarantor named, and the regulated subsidiaries must keep minimum capital of about USD 3.0 billion. That structure removes sponsor extraction risk but also any sponsor backstop, and it makes noteholders structurally dependent on subsidiary dividends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is visible only through contract terms. Premiums are fixed per member and actuarially sound by requirement, but they are re-set annually while cost trend moves continuously, which is why the ratio rose even though premium revenue for Medicaid was unchanged for the nine months. Membership is falling (down 11.46% since year-end), so premium revenue fell 4% in the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 33; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins cannot be defended by cost cutting alone. Medical care costs are about 92% of premium and the G&A ratio rose to 6.8% for the nine months from 6.5% as premium fell, so operating leverage is adverse: a change of less than one percentage point in the medical care ratio equals all of last-twelve-months EBITDA. The company holds some levers, notably suspending buybacks, exiting the MAPD product and repricing Marketplace, but each shrinks revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24, 26, 30; calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low (capital spending of USD 101 million in FY2025), so EBITDA converts to cash easily in a normal year, but the conversion has been negative in the worst periods because government settlements, tax payments and claims timing swing operating cash flow by hundreds of millions. FY2025 operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 535 million on EBITDA of USD 976 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is the dominant force: the buyers are state agencies and the federal government, which set rates and rebid contracts, so Molina has little pricing power and its margin depends on rate adequacy. Supplier power sits with providers and drug suppliers, where outpatient and high-cost drug categories drove the Medicaid ratio up. Rivalry takes the form of procurement competition and sector consolidation, and entry barriers are regulatory and procurement-based, so new entrants are a limited threat. Policy is the primary external driver: the federal budget law is expected to cut Medicaid enrolment gradually from 2027 and reduce premium by 2% to 3% a year through 2029, and Marketplace rule changes have shrunk that book. For creditors the sector translates into a slow-moving but one-way risk to revenue and a rate-lag risk to margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are scale, low capital intensity, a maturity profile with nothing due before 2028 and a record of winning state contracts; the weaknesses are thin margins, parent dependence on regulated subsidiaries, state concentration and shrinking membership; the opportunities that matter are rate updates that catch up with cost trend and new contracts in Florida, Illinois and Wisconsin; the threats are further rate lag, loss of a large-state contract and policy-driven enrolment loss.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the revenue base is expected to shrink further (Medicaid to about 4.4 million members by year-end excluding the new Florida enrolment, Marketplace to about 250,000, Medicare to about 230,000) while new contracts start between 2026-10-01 and 2027-01-01, and the first-quarter 2026 impairment and the fourth-quarter 2025 loss drop out of the reported figures. Over three to five years the federal budget law reduces Medicaid expansion enrolment gradually and limits provider tax financing from 2028, and management targets premium and earnings growth of 11% to 13% that is not supported by figures in the documents. The credit implication is that deleveraging depends on margin recovery rather than debt paydown, because nothing matures before 2028 and the notes are not prepayable from free cash flow at this scale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is that state rate updates for 2027 do not keep pace with medical cost trend while the favourable prior-year reserve development seen in 2026 does not repeat. The first operational break is the medical care ratio: without the USD 352 million of reserve release the nine-month EBITDA would have been USD 99 million and last-twelve-months EBITDA an outflow of USD 19 million, before any offset from minimum medical loss ratio rules and cost corridors. That feeds through subsidiary earnings to dividends: about USD 170 million can be paid without approval against annual coupons that are higher, so the parent would draw on its USD 608 million of cash, which covers about 33.99 months of accrued interest at the 2026 pace. Leverage would be undefined on a negative EBITDA and the interest cover test, already cut to 1.75x, would be the observable trigger; if it were breached the undrawn revolver could become unavailable and a covenant default under it could in turn engage the cross-default terms of the notes, although the filings do not give the definitions or thresholds. Management levers are suspending buybacks, repricing or exiting products, and capital moves between subsidiaries. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity event in the next twelve months, because of the USD 8,579 million of unrestricted cash and investments and no maturity before 2028, but not sufficient to hold its current credit quality if the ratio keeps rising.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_moh-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C7; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strengths are a maturity profile with nothing due before 2028 and an undrawn revolver, which means a refinancing event is not the near-term test; low capital intensity, with capital spending of USD 101 million against USD 45,426 million of revenue; the suspension of buybacks and the rise in parent cash to USD 608 million; a record of renewing and winning state contracts, in management's words; and audited, transparent reporting that lets creditors see where the weakness is.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The weaknesses are margins that depend on a ratio the company does not set and that has moved from 90.8% to 92.1% in a year; leverage of 11.32x on last-twelve-months EBITDA with accrued interest cover of 1.56x; concentration, with Medicaid at 74.89% and four states at 40.23% of premium revenue; a parent that relies on subsidiary dividends and holds a small part of group cash; and shrinking membership with policy headwinds through 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Molina presents a business profile of adequate scale supported by contract-based government revenue, a maturity profile with no principal due before 2028 and low capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by margins that have collapsed with the medical care ratio, concentration in Medicaid and four states, and a parent that owes all the debt while most cash sits in regulated plans. Cash-flow durability appears weak at present because operating cash flow swings with settlement timing and reported earnings include reserve releases. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on whether the medical care ratio recovers before 2028 and on the coupon needed to replace notes now carrying low rates. The primary downside path is medical costs outrunning premium rates while membership falls. Further analysis would require the credit agreement definitions, the proxy statement, market prices of the notes and management's 2027 plan. Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: the medical care ratio.
